resale_co.name: Zoning Compliance Certification (homes built after January 1, 1996 only)
resale_co.issued_by: City of Ocean City (requested on the same sale-of-property inspection application; Zoning Office)
requirements: Zoning compliance check at the in-person sale inspection, for homes built after January 1, 1996
resale_co.how_to_apply: Use the City's Sale of Property inspection application (the same form as the smoke/CO certificate); give the date of the final CO (year built) so the City knows zoning certification is needed. Send it to 115 12th Street, Ocean City, NJ 08226, (609) 399-6111 x 9727, smokedetector@ocnj.us.

evidence.quote: Homes built after January 1, 1996 also require Zoning Compliance Certification.
The inspection fee is $50 per unit for properties built before 1996 or $100 per unit if the property was built after 1996.
Fenton, Jessica - Zoning Official Email: jfenton@ocnj.us Phone: 609-399-6111;9759

resale_co.notes: The City's 2025 sale-of-property application says homes built after January 1, 1996 also require Zoning Compliance Certification, and the same form charges $100 per unit for post-1996 homes versus $50 for older homes. It appears to be one combined in-person inspection and one fee (recorded under fire_cert, not repeated here), but the form does not say how the $100 splits or whether the Zoning Office issues a separate certificate. Homes built before 1996 need only the smoke/CO certificate as far as the form shows. No other resale certificate of occupancy or housing inspection was found; the Zoning Fees sheet (2017) lists no resale item. Ocean City licenses rental properties (and requires lead-based paint inspections of pre-1978 rentals of 6 months or more); those are rental programs. Zoning Office general line 609-399-6111 x9758, zoning@ocnj.us.

requirements: Homes built before 1977: 10-year sealed battery smoke alarms on each level and outside each sleeping area
Built January 1977 to February 21, 1983: hardwired (120 volt) smoke alarms on each level and near each sleeping area (interconnection not required)
Built February 22, 1983 to April 30, 1993: hardwired multi-station smoke alarms on each level and near each sleeping area, interconnected
Built May 1, 1993 to present: hardwired interconnected smoke alarms with battery backup in all bedrooms, outside each sleeping area and on every level
CO alarms (UL 2034) near sleeping areas when there are fuel-burning devices or an attached garage

Portable fire extinguisher 2A-10B:C for the sale of 1-2 family units, on its bracket within 10 feet of the kitchen in the path of egress, top no more than 5 feet up (City requirements sheet dated February 2024, before P.L.2025, c.19)
Inspections are in person only; self-certifications are no longer accepted
Individually owned condo units in multifamily buildings also need the certificate

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Inspection Request: Sale of Property Application for Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance (closing date, requested inspection date and time, access: meet owner/agent/tenant or lock box code, buyer and agent details, year of final CO). Submit to 115 12th Street, Ocean City, NJ 08226, call 609-399-6111 ext. 9727, or email smokedetector@ocnj.us. Payment by mail, in person or online. The seller or the seller's agent must get it before the sale or transfer of title.

evidence.quote: Certification is required for all residential rental units in one- and two-family dwellings and for the sale or transfer of title of residential units in one- and two-family dwellings, and individually owned condo units in multiple dwellings.

All inspections must be done in-person. Self-certifications are no longer being accepted. To schedule an inspection, please use the forms provided below, call 609-399-6111 ext. 9727, and/or email smokedetector@ocnj.us with any questions.

Certification must be obtained by the seller or their authorized agent prior to property sale or transfer of title for all residential units within 1 and 2 family dwellings, and individually-owned condo units within a multifamily structure.
Fire extinguishers are required in all yearly rentals and for the sale of all units within 1 and 2 family dwellings.
Smoke Detector Certification: Apply for certificate of smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance. 609-399-6111 x9727 or smokedetector@ocnj.us

fire_cert.notes: Ocean City is state-enforced for the Uniform Fire Code (DCA registry code S), but the DCA's July 2026 list of state-enforced towns does not mark Ocean City 'SC', meaning the State does not issue smoke certificates there; the City's own Division of Fire Prevention issues them. The state fire directory (survey 2/13/2025) lists 'NJ Division Fire Safety' under Smoke Detector Compliance for Ocean City; the City's pages and 2025 form are newer and are followed here. No named fire prevention official was found on the City site; the Ocean City Fire Department (Chief Bernard Walker, 609-525-9182, bwalker@ocnj.us) is the fire/rescue department, not the smoke certificate office. The City's older 'Smoke Detector' page still links a 2020 self-certification form, but the Fire Prevention FAQ says self-certifications are no longer accepted. No late or rush fee tiers are shown on the 2025 form.
